description: Edit recorded lessons, review a live preview, and deliver video with captions.

tools.name: account_get
tools.description: The signed-in user, their workspace and role in it, the workspace's plan (and when a trial ends) and its agent credits: the balance, the monthly allowance and the packages an owner can buy. Use it to tell when a request needs a paid plan or more credits. Returns the GetAccountResponse.

tools.name: agent-chats_list
tools.description: The editor agent chats in a video, most recently active first, each with its `status` and `lastReply`. Poll it to follow a chat you started: `idle` means its turn ended. Required: videoId. Returns array of AgentChat.

params.name: videoId
params.description: The video whose agent chats to list

tools.name: agent-chats_start
tools.description: Start a chat with Tella's editor agent in a video you can edit, as if you had typed `prompt` in its agent chat; without `videoId` it first makes a new, empty video. The agent works in the background and spends the workspace's AI Credits. Follow it with `GET /v1/agent-chats?videoId=`. Required: prompt. Optional: name, videoId. Returns the new StartAgentChatResponse.

params.name: name
params.description: The new video's name. Only used without `videoId`; left out, the prompt's start names it.

params.name: prompt

params.name: videoId

tools.name: auto-captures_reports_auto-capture
tools.description: Tell Tella that a take went wrong, so the cause gets found and fixed in Auto Capture. That covers what it filmed (the wrong page or feature, a step that was asked for missed or cut off, stopping short of the result) and how the recording came out (choppy playback, frozen or black frames, a cursor that doesn't match what happened). Reporting changes nothing on the take, starts nothing and costs nothing; to get a better take, revise it over the MCP server. A take can be reported more than once, by the person who started it or anyone in the workspace it was made in. A take that is still running can't be reported (400). Any other source, or a take you can't see, answers 404. Required: sourceId, reason. Returns the new AutoCaptureReport.

params.name: sourceId
params.description: The take's `sourceId`

params.name: reason
params.description: What went wrong, in the user's words when they gave them: what the take shows against what was asked, or how the recording plays. Never a password, code or sign-in link.

tools.name: backgrounds_list
tools.description: Returns personal uploads, workspace uploads, and Tella's default image and animated backgrounds in named categories. Each item includes a preview URL and a background value that can be passed directly to the clip update endpoint. Optional: scope, categoryId.

params.name: scope
params.description: Filter by scope

params.name: categoryId
params.description: Filter by category ID, such as personal, workspace, default:tella, default:macos, or default:animated

tools.name: library_capture-screenshot
tools.description: Deprecated: use `POST /v1/library/imports`, which takes the same `url` and `scroll` and also imports video links. Captures a public web page or a single post on X, Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok and saves it to the caller's private library. Pages are captured above the fold; social posts are cropped to their embed card. Set scroll=true to record a scrolling web page as video (ignored for social posts). Returns a finished image or video library item with a sourceId for overlays or layout media. Unlike AI generation, capture completes in this request, with no polling; allow up to two minutes. Private pages and social profiles/feeds are not supported. Use an Idempotency-Key when retrying to avoid duplicate captures. Required: url. Optional: scroll.

params.name: scroll
params.description: Record a scrolling web page as video instead of a still (default false). Ignored for social posts.

params.name: url
params.description: Public web page or single post on X, Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok. A missing scheme defaults to HTTPS.

tools.name: library_create-generation
tools.description: Starts generating an image, a short video clip or a sound effect from a text prompt with the same AI generators the editor's media panels use. Generation is asynchronous: the response is a `generation` whose `id` is the private library item the result is saved as. Poll `GET /v1/library/generations/{id}` every few seconds (images usually take 30-90 seconds, sound effects 10-30, video several minutes) until `status` is `completed`, then pass `item.sourceId` anywhere a source is accepted — `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/overlays` for an image or video overlay, `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/layouts` with `media` for b-roll, `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/sound-effects` for a sound effect. The finished item also appears in `GET /v1/library?scope=private`. Each generation counts against the caller's weekly AI generation allowance, which depends on the plan; exceeding it answers 403 with the reset time. A video is also charged in the workspace's AI Credits and is refused with a 403 while the balance is empty. Required: prompt, type. Optional: durationSeconds, model, referenceSourceId. Returns the new CreateGenerationResponse.

params.name: durationSeconds
params.description: For `video` only: the clip's length in whole seconds, 4-30 on `seedance-2.5` and 4-15 on the 2.0 models. Defaults to 5. A longer clip costs proportionally more credits and takes longer to generate.

params.name: model
params.description: Which model to use. For `image`, a GPT Image 2.6 model: `sunburst` (default) is the most capable and follows reference images most precisely; `flare` is faster. For `video`, a Seedance model: `seedance-2.5` is the default and has the best quality (1080p); `seedance-2.0-fast` is quicker and cheaper (720p); `seedance-2.0-mini` is the cheapest (720p). Not accepted for `sound-effect`.

params.name: prompt
params.description: What to generate. Up to 4000 characters for an image, 2000 for a video or a sound effect.

params.name: referenceSourceId
params.description: For `image` and `video` only: the `sourceId` of an image source to guide the generation — from `POST /v1/sources` (`kind: 'image'`) after uploading the bytes, or an `image` library item's `sourceId`.

params.name: type
params.description: The kind of media to generate

tools.name: library_create-item
tools.description: Saves an uploaded source to the library so it can be listed and reused later, both here and in the editor's media panels. Create the source via `POST /v1/sources` and upload the bytes first, then pass its `sourceId`. Without this a source is only reachable through the clips that already reference it. To bring in an image you saved in a connected Pinterest, Are.na or mymind account instead, pass `from` with the service and `sourceId` set to the item's `id` from `GET /v1/library?scope=<service>`; Tella copies the image into your `private` library (default), the `workspace` library, or with `scope: 'video'` the library of the video named by `videoId`. Only images can be brought in: Pinterest image pins, Are.na image blocks, and mymind images or the screenshot mymind took of a saved page. Required: sourceId. Optional: from, name, scope (plus 2 more). Returns the new CreateLibraryItemResponse.

params.name: from
params.description: Bring an image in from your connected Pinterest, Are.na or mymind account, or a shot from Tella's `vintage` film catalog, instead of saving an uploaded source. Tella copies it, and the returned item's `sourceId` places it like any other image or video.

params.name: name
params.description: Display name shown in the library. Defaults to the item's type, or for a `vintage` shot, the film's title and year.

params.name: scope
params.description: Where to save the item (default: `private`). `workspace` shares it with everyone in the workspace and requires an owner or member role; viewers get a 403. `video`, with `from` set to `pinterest`, `arena` or `mymind` only, saves it to the library of the video named by `videoId`.

params.name: sourceId
params.description: Source ID from `POST /v1/sources`, with the bytes already uploaded to its `uploadUrl`. With `from`, the `id` of an item from `GET /v1/library?scope=<from>` instead.

params.name: type
params.description: Expected item type. Optional — the type is taken from the source's own kind; supplying a value that disagrees is an error.

params.name: videoId
params.description: With `from` and `scope: 'video'`: the video whose media library the image is saved to. Requires edit access to that video.

tools.name: library_delete-item
tools.description: Removes an item from the library. This removes the library entry only — clips already using the underlying source keep working. Required: id, scope. Returns the SuccessResponse. Destructive.

params.name: id
params.description: Library item ID

params.name: scope
params.description: Which library the item belongs to: `workspace` items are shared with everyone in the workspace, `private` items are only visible to their creator

tools.name: library_get-generation
tools.description: Returns the current status of a generation started with `POST /v1/library/generations`. Poll until `status` is `completed` (then `item` holds the finished library item) or `failed` (then `error` says why; start a new generation). Required: id.

params.name: id
params.description: Generation ID — the `generation.id` returned when it was started

tools.name: library_get-import
tools.description: Returns the status of an import started with `POST /v1/library/imports`. Pass the same `videoId` it was started with. Poll until `status` is `completed` (then `item` holds the library item) or `failed` (then `error` says why; start a new import to retry). Required: id. Optional: videoId.

params.name: id
params.description: Import ID — the `import.id` returned when it was started

params.name: videoId
params.description: The `videoId` the import was started with, if any

tools.name: library_list-items
tools.description: Returns a page of reusable media saved to the library — images, videos, screenshots, sound effects, music and LUTs — for one scope. Items added through the API include a `sourceId` you can pass anywhere a source is accepted, including images. Editor-added images, screenshots, music and LUTs expose a hosted `url` instead. URL captures from `POST /v1/library/screenshots` are placeable `image` or `video` items. Media still being generated in the editor is omitted. `scope=default` returns Tella's curated sound effect and background music catalogs instead of stored media: those items carry a `presetId` to place them with (`sound-effect` items via `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/sound-effects`, `music` items via `PUT /v1/videos/{id}/background-music`), a `category`, and a publicly fetchable `url` for previewing, and arrive as a single page; filter with `type=sound-effect` or `type=music`, or omit `type` for both. Tella's default backgrounds are not part of this catalog — they are placed as a background rather than as a source, and are listed by `GET /v1/backgrounds`. `scope=pinterest`, `scope=arena` and `scope=mymind` list the images you saved in that service once you connect it under Settings → Connections: your newest saves, or matches for `query`, as one page. Their `id` is the service's own ID; bring one into Tella with `POST /v1/library` and `from` before placing it. A service you haven't connected returns 503 `unavailable`. Required: scope. Optional: type, query, collection (plus 2 more).

params.name: scope
params.description: Which set of media to read: `private` (only visible to their creator), `workspace` (shared with everyone in the workspace), `default` (Tella's curated sound effect and background music catalogs, which hold no other media type), `pinterest`, `arena` or `mymind` (the images you saved in that service, once you connect it under Settings → Connections), or `vintage` (Tella's catalog of public-domain vintage film shots). Bring a `pinterest`, `arena`, `mymind` or `vintage` item in with `POST /v1/library` and `from`.

params.name: type
params.description: Only return items of this type. With `scope=default` only `sound-effect` and `music` are valid, since the curated catalog holds no other media type; omitting it returns both.

params.name: query
params.description: With `scope=pinterest`, `arena`, `mymind` or `vintage` only: words to search for. Omit to list your newest saves, or with `vintage`, to browse featured films.

params.name: collection
params.description: With `scope=pinterest`, `arena` or `mymind` only: one of your boards, channels or spaces, by its name, id or address (an Are.na channel can be anyone's public one). Lists its images, and adds the `collection` with its description to the response; `query` is ignored.

params.name: cursor
params.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Keep paging while `cursor` is present. `scope=default` is a fixed catalog, and `pinterest`, `arena` and `mymind` return a single page of your newest saves or best matches, so they never set one. `vintage` pages through its results.

params.name: limit
params.description: Items per page (1-60, default 24). Treat it as a target rather than an exact count: pages are read from storage before unlistable items are filtered out, and cursors address whole storage pages, so a response may contain somewhat more than `limit`. Returning the extra items is deliberate — trimming them would drop them, because the cursor has already moved past.

tools.name: library_start-import
tools.description: Brings media into Tella from a link. A public web page is captured above the fold at 1920×1080 (or, with `scroll=true`, recorded scrolling as video); a single post on X, Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok is cropped to its embed card. These finish in this request (allow up to two minutes) and answer 201 with `status: completed`. A link to a single video is downloaded in the background and answers 202 with `status: running`: poll `GET /v1/library/imports/{id}?videoId=…` every 5-10 seconds until it is `completed` or `failed`. Video links need `videoId` and land in that video's library; everything else lands in your private library unless you pass `videoId`. Place `item.sourceId` as an overlay or layout media. Only import media you own or have the rights to use. Private pages, social profiles and feeds, and private, members-only or age-restricted videos are not supported. Use an Idempotency-Key when retrying to avoid duplicate imports. Required: url. Optional: scroll, video, videoId. Returns the new ImportResponse.

params.name: scroll
params.description: Record a scrolling web page as video instead of a still (default false). Ignored for social posts and video links.

params.name: url
params.description: A public web page, a single post on X, Instagram, LinkedIn or TikTok, or a link to a single video on YouTube, X, Instagram or TikTok. A missing scheme defaults to HTTPS.

params.name: video
params.description: Omit to download every video link, and X and Instagram `/p/` posts that hold a video. `false` captures the link's page or card instead; `true` downloads a post without checking first that it holds one.

params.name: videoId
params.description: Save into this video's own library instead of your private library. You must be able to edit it. Required for video downloads.

tools.name: motion_apply-commands
tools.description: Applies a batch of ops and the editor's own commands as one transaction and one undo step; nothing applies unless everything does. Prefer a command for anything the editor does (titles, shapes, media, keyframes and easing, effects, masks, text animation, fades), since it keeps the editor's conventions; use ops (`node.patch`, `node.move`, `node.insert`, …) for the rest. `GET /v1/motion/schema?schema=edits&type=…` gives each one's fields. Pass `baseRevision` to refuse the batch with 409 if the document changed since you read it, and `dryRun` to check it without saving. Required: id, commands. Optional: baseRevision, dryRun. Returns the new MotionApplyResult.

params.name: id
params.description: Tella Motion document ID (ffd_…), from `GET /v1/motion/documents`.

params.name: baseRevision
params.description: The `seq` you inspected. The batch is refused with 409 when the document has changed since.

params.name: commands
params.description: Commands

params.name: dryRun
params.description: Check the batch without saving it.

With `documentId` and no `videoId`, it makes a new video for the document, as large as its canvas, and returns its `videoId` and `editUrl`. Build what it shows with `POST /v1/motion/documents/{id}/commands`. The clip routes that edit layouts, cuts, zooms, overlays or the transcript refuse a Tella Motion clip; it can still be renamed, moved and deleted. Required: name. Optional: documentId, duration, videoId.

params.description: A Tella Motion document of yours that no video plays yet, for the clip to play instead of a blank one. The video takes it over.

params.name: duration
params.description: How long the clip plays, in seconds (default 10): the blank document's canvas length. Not with `documentId`, whose document keeps its own length.

params.name: name
params.description: The clip's name, and the new video's when there is no `videoId`.

params.name: videoId
params.description: The video (vid_…) to add the clip to. Leave it out, with `documentId`, for a new video.

tools.name: motion_create-document
tools.description: Creates a blank document, 10 s long (the `canvas.set` op changes that). With `videoId` it is the video's, as large as the video unless sized, for an overlay or b-roll you build in place. Without it the document is yours and in no video yet (1920×1080 unless sized); the first video it is placed in takes it over. Edit it with `POST /v1/motion/documents/{id}/commands`, then show it with `POST /v1/videos/{id}/clips/{clipId}/overlays` (`motionDocumentId`) or a layout's `media: {type: 'motion', documentId}`. It plays there live, so later edits show in the video as you make them. Required: name. Optional: height, videoId, width. Returns the new MotionDocumentResponse.

params.name: height
params.description: Canvas height in pixels. Defaults to the video's, or 1080 without a video.

params.name: name
params.description: What it shows.

params.name: videoId

params.name: width
params.description: Canvas width in pixels. Defaults to the video's, or 1920 without a video.

tools.name: motion_download-document

tools.name: videos_clips_update-transcript-words
tools.description: Correct what a clip's transcript says, one or more words at a time (at most 100 per request). Each edit addresses a word by its transcript `index` and sets either `text` (the corrected wording, which also unhides the word) or `hidden` (whether the word appears in captions and subtitles). Edits change the transcript, captions and subtitles only — never the audio or the clip's timing; use cut-by-transcript to remove spoken words from the video. Visibility and wording are independent: hiding a word preserves any correction made to it. The whole batch is applied atomically as a single transaction, so a request never changes only some of its words. A `500` does not by itself mean nothing changed — the words can land and a later step of the commit still fail — so treat the outcome as either fully applied or not applied at all. Every edit assigns a word outright, so re-sending the identical request is safe and settles it. Required: id, clipId, words. Returns array of TranscriptWord.

tools.name: videos_publish_video
tools.description: Posts the video to one of your connected social accounts: YouTube, YouTube Shorts, LinkedIn, X, Instagram (post, reel or story) or Facebook (post or story). This posts under your own account, so check the destination, text and privacy before calling it. It uploads an export with the `export` settings, reusing a finished or running one or starting one, so there is no need to export first. The account must already be connected in Tella (Settings → Connections, or Share → Publish in the editor); a 403 means it isn't, or that the plan doesn't include the export's resolution or frame rate. With several accounts connected for a destination, pass `accountId` from GET /v1/social-accounts; without it the oldest connected one posts. To post to several accounts, call once per account. TikTok can only be published from the Tella app, because TikTok requires its consent form. Returns 202 with a `queued` publication, which stays `queued` while the export renders; poll GET /v1/videos/{id}/publish for the result. To post later, pass `scheduledAt`: the publication stays `queued` with that `scheduledAt` until then, and DELETE /v1/videos/{id}/publish cancels it before it goes out. One publish per destination and account runs at a time. Requires edit access to the video. Required: id, destination, title. Optional: accountId, description, export (plus 3 more).

params.name: id
params.description: Unique video identifier

params.name: accountId
params.description: Which of your connected accounts to post with, from GET /v1/social-accounts. Defaults to the oldest connected account for the destination.

params.name: description
params.description: YouTube description, or the post text on LinkedIn, X, Instagram and Facebook.

params.name: destination
params.description: Where to post. YouTube Shorts must be vertical or square and at most 3 minutes; Facebook Stories vertical and at most 60 seconds; Facebook Reels vertical and at most 90 seconds; Instagram Stories at most 60 seconds and 100 MB; Instagram posts and reels at most 15 minutes and 300 MB; no Instagram destination takes a 4K export; LinkedIn at most 30 minutes and 500 MB. Instagram, Facebook Stories and Reels and LinkedIn need at least 3 seconds. YouTube takes at most 15 minutes from a channel that isn't verified; X at most 20 minutes, or 125 with Premium or a checkmark. Stories show no text. The Facebook and Instagram destinations publish through one Facebook connection.

novel_features.name: Cross-video transcript search
novel_features.description: FTS5 search across cached clip transcripts; returns video and clip references with matching text snippets.

novel_features.name: Watch-milestone digest

novel_features.name: Webhook tail + replay
novel_features.description: webhooks tail streams or snapshots inbox events; webhooks replay separately replays prior messages to a local URL with valid HMAC headers.

novel_features.name: Bulk standard edit pass
novel_features.description: Plan or apply public filler, buffer, edge and silence edits across playlist clips; use find-retakes for transcript retakes and agent-chats for semantic edits.

novel_features.name: Transcript diff (cut vs uncut)
novel_features.description: Diff a clip's cut transcript against its uncut transcript to surface every word that editing removed (filler, silence, hand-edit) with timecodes.

novel_features.name: Upload-to-edit workflow
novel_features.description: Create a Tella source and upload local media bytes to its pre-signed URL then return the source ID; use videos clips insert-file to upload and attach media to a video.

novel_features.name: Exports waitlist
novel_features.description: Kick off exports for one or more videos and poll GET /v1/videos/{id}/exports/{exportId}, reporting progress and the download URL. Exit non-zero if an export fails or times out.

novel_features.name: Caption-file export
novel_features.description: Format a clip's cut transcript as an SRT or VTT subtitle file ready to attach to an embed or upload.

novel_features.name: Workspace stats
novel_features.description: Local aggregate of video count, clip count, total duration, transcript word count, and export count by month across the cached workspace.

novel_features.name: Declarative video storyboard
novel_features.description: Export editable video timeline and state only; use videos apply-storyboard --file PLAN.json --apply to apply a reviewed JSON edit plan.

novel_features.name: One-shot media insertion
novel_features.description: Upload local media into a Tella source and attach it as a clip; use videos clips add-broll for B-roll layout media.

novel_features.name: Transcript-driven repairs
novel_features.description: Plan or apply term-matched transcript-index cuts; use videos clips replace-word-ranges for replacement media.

novel_features.name: Pre-publish edit QA
novel_features.description: Scan a video timeline for likely issues such as long silences before export or sharing.

novel_features.name: Playlist-scale edit planning
novel_features.description: Plan a standard remove-fillers/remove-buffers/trim-edges/export recipe across every video in a playlist.

novel_features.name: Safe clip clean workflow
novel_features.description: Plan or apply official per-clip cleanup with automatic pre-apply cut snapshots and explicit recovery.

novel_features.name: Cut rollback workflow
novel_features.description: Restore a saved cuts snapshot (latest by default or selected with --snapshot); use videos clips restore-cuts for inline cuts JSON and retain divergence checks and exclusive-editing confirmation.

novel_features.name: Automatic video edit pass
novel_features.description: Apply selected automatic edits across clips with recovery snapshots and finish with a live preview.

novel_features.name: House-style lesson preparation
novel_features.description: Prepare a lesson from a validated recipe and finish with a preview for review.

novel_features.name: Reviewed lesson delivery
novel_features.description: Export, wait, and download a lesson MP4 and SRT or VTT captions.

novel_features.name: Conservative retake plan
novel_features.description: Propose repeated sentence cuts with timestamps and apply reviewed cuts under snapshots.

novel_features.name: Review storyboard files
novel_features.description: Save video, clip, or source storyboard images for visual inspection.
